newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq TV shows Baghdad house hit by U.S. missile.
newsitem.headline: Iraq TV shows Baghdad house hit by U.S. missile.

text.p: Iraqi state-run television showed a damaged house on Tuesday which it said it was hit by a U.S. cruise missile fired at targets in Iraq in response to Baghdad's thrust into the Kurdish north of the country.
The television showed the flat concrete roof of the one-storey house caved in by the explosion but said there were no casualties.
Interviewing an eyewitness, it said the building was in one of the residential quarters of Baghdad but did not say where the house was exactly located.

U.S. defence officials said 27 cruise missiles were fired earlier on Tuesday at about 15 targets in southern Iraq including air defence radars, missile sites and command and communication centres. Baghdad was not among the targets mentioned by U.S. officials.
An Iraqi military spokesman said five people were killed and 19 wounded in the U.S. cruise missile strike.

Iraq said its troops had sided with rebels of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) of Massoud Barzani on Saturday and helped them win control of Arbil from querrillas of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) of Jalal Talabani.

Iraq's intervention in Kurdistan prompted the United States to fire the missiles, impose further restrictions on flights by Iraqi aircraft and put off implementation of an oil-for-food plan Iraq had signed with the United Nations on May 20.
Iraqi television also showed several thousand Iraqis in the northern city of Mosul, 400 km (260 miles) north of Baghdad, protesting against the U.S. attack.
A television caption read: "The angry masses of Arbil, Dohouk and Sulaimaniya are protesting against America's unjust aggression."
The protesters carried banners which read: "Against the will of America, Kurds and Arabs are fighting together", "Yes, Yes for wars" and "We sacrifice our souls for you Saddam."
